claim: Drug resistance is a challenge in anticancer therapy.
source: Drug resistance is a challenge in anticancer therapy.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field supported by established scientific consensus.

claim: Cancers can possess intrinsic drug resistance prior to drug exposure.
source: In many cases, cancers can be resistant to the drug prior to exposure, that is, possess intrinsic drug resistance.
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific knowledge about drug resistance mechanisms.

claim: We lack target-independent methods to anticipate resistance in cancer cell lines or characterize intrinsic drug resistance without a priori knowledge of its cause.
source: However, we lack target-independent methods to anticipate resistance in cancer cell lines or characterize intrinsic drug resistance without a priori knowledge of its cause.
evidence: This statement describes a gap in current methodology, representing established knowledge about limitations in the field.

claim: Cell morphology could provide an unbiased readout of drug resistance.
source: We hypothesized that cell morphology could provide an unbiased readout of drug resistance.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as the hypothesis of the study.

claim: HCT116 cells are a mismatch repair-deficient cancer cell line.
source: To test this hypothesis, we used HCT116 cells, a mismatch repair-deficient cancer cell line, to isolate clones that were resistant or sensitive to bortezomib, a well-characterized proteasome inhibitor and anticancer drug to which many cancer cells possess intrinsic resistance.
evidence: This is a known characteristic of HCT116 cells supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Bortezomib is a well-characterized proteasome inhibitor and anticancer drug.
source: To test this hypothesis, we used HCT116 cells, a mismatch repair-deficient cancer cell line, to isolate clones that were resistant or sensitive to bortezomib, a well-characterized proteasome inhibitor and anticancer drug to which many cancer cells possess intrinsic resistance.
evidence: This is established knowledge about bortezomib's mechanism and clinical use.

claim: Many cancer cells possess intrinsic resistance to bortezomib.
source: To test this hypothesis, we used HCT116 cells, a mismatch repair-deficient cancer cell line, to isolate clones that were resistant or sensitive to bortezomib, a well-characterized proteasome inhibitor and anticancer drug to which many cancer cells possess intrinsic resistance.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge about bortezomib resistance.

claim: The imaging- and computation-based profiling pipeline identified morphological features that differed between resistant and sensitive cells.
source: Our imaging- and computation-based profiling pipeline identified morphological features that differed between resistant and sensitive cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: A morphological signature of bortezomib resistance was generated from features that differed between resistant and sensitive cells.
source: We used these features to generate a morphological signature of bortezomib resistance.
evidence: This describes a key methodological outcome of the study based on the experimental data.

claim: The morphological signature correctly predicted sensitivity to bortezomib in seven out of ten cases not included in the signature training dataset, in the absence of drug treatment.
source: We then employed this morphological signature to analyze a set of HCT116 clones (five resistant and five sensitive) that had not been included in the signature training dataset, and correctly predicted sensitivity to bortezomib in seven cases, in the absence of drug treatment.
evidence: This is a primary experimental result supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The morphological signature predicted bortezomib resistance better than resistance to other drugs targeting the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
source: This signature predicted bortezomib resistance better than resistance to other drugs targeting the ubiquitin-proteasome system, indicating specificity for mechanisms of resistance to bortezomib.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data comparing performance across different drugs.

claim: The morphological signature has specificity for mechanisms of resistance to bortezomib.
source: This signature predicted bortezomib resistance better than resistance to other drugs targeting the ubiquitin-proteasome system, indicating specificity for mechanisms of resistance to bortezomib.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential performance of the signature on bortezomib versus other UPS-targeting drugs.

claim: The results establish a proof-of-concept framework for the unbiased analysis of drug resistance using high-content microscopy of cancer cells, in the absence of drug treatment.
source: Our results establish a proof-of-concept framework for the unbiased analysis of drug resistance using high-content microscopy of cancer cells, in the absence of drug treatment.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental results presented in the study.

claim: Targeted cancer therapies often fail due to drug resistance.
source: Targeted cancer therapies often fail due to drug resistance, which makes determining the drug sensitivity of populations of cancer cells requisite for timely and effective treatment (Garraway and Jänne, 2012; Pisa and Kapoor, 2020; Vasan et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Determining the drug sensitivity of populations of cancer cells is requisite for timely and effective treatment.
source: Targeted cancer therapies often fail due to drug resistance, which makes determining the drug sensitivity of populations of cancer cells requisite for timely and effective treatment (Garraway and Jänne, 2012; Pisa and Kapoor, 2020; Vasan et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Resistance can be categorized as acquired, manifesting in the context of prolonged treatment, or intrinsic, pre-existing in the cancer cell population.
source: Resistance is complex and can be categorized as acquired, manifesting in the context of prolonged treatment, or intrinsic, pre-existing in the cancer cell population (Gottesman et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Most studies of resistance focus on the drug's known target(s) or expression levels of drug efflux pumps.
source: Most studies of resistance focus on the drug's known target(s) or expression levels of drug efflux pumps (Garraway and Jänne, 2012; Gottesman et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: We currently lack unbiased methods of identifying drug resistance in cells especially prior to treatment.
source: However, we currently lack unbiased methods of identifying drug resistance in cells especially prior to treatment.
evidence: This statement describes a gap in current methodology based on established knowledge.

claim: Bortezomib is an anticancer drug commonly used to treat multiple myeloma.
source: Bortezomib is an anticancer drug commonly used to treat multiple myeloma and nearly half of multiple myeloma patients show no initial response to bortezomib therapy, indicating intrinsic resistance (Chen et al., 2011; Gonzalez-Santamarta et al., 2020; Mitsiades et al., 2004; Hideshima et al., 2001; Vincenz et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Nearly half of multiple myeloma patients show no initial response to bortezomib therapy, indicating intrinsic resistance.
source: Bortezomib is an anticancer drug commonly used to treat multiple myeloma and nearly half of multiple myeloma patients show no initial response to bortezomib therapy, indicating intrinsic resistance (Chen et al., 2011; Gonzalez-Santamarta et al., 2020; Mitsiades et al., 2004; Hideshima et al., 2001; Vincenz et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Bortezomib resistance can be attributed to mutations in the bortezomib-binding pocket of the proteasome subunit (PSMB5).
source: Bortezomib resistance can be attributed to targeted mechanisms such as mutations in the bortezomib-binding pocket of the proteasome subunit (PSMB5) and overexpression of proteasome subunits (Barrio et al., 2019; Franke et al., 2012; van de Ven et al., 2008; Wacker et al., 2012) as well as non-specific mechanisms, such as upregulation of prosurvival or anti-apoptotic pathways and enhanced cell adhesion to the extracellular matrix (Gonzalez-Santamarta et al., 2020; Hideshima et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Bortezomib resistance can be attributed to overexpression of proteasome subunits.
source: Bortezomib resistance can be attributed to targeted mechanisms such as mutations in the bortezomib-binding pocket of the proteasome subunit (PSMB5) and overexpression of proteasome subunits (Barrio et al., 2019; Franke et al., 2012; van de Ven et al., 2008; Wacker et al., 2012) as well as non-specific mechanisms, such as upregulation of prosurvival or anti-apoptotic pathways and enhanced cell adhesion to the extracellular matrix (Gonzalez-Santamarta et al., 2020; Hideshima et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Bortezomib resistance can be attributed to upregulation of prosurvival or anti-apoptotic pathways.
source: Bortezomib resistance can be attributed to targeted mechanisms such as mutations in the bortezomib-binding pocket of the proteasome subunit (PSMB5) and overexpression of proteasome subunits (Barrio et al., 2019; Franke et al., 2012; van de Ven et al., 2008; Wacker et al., 2012) as well as non-specific mechanisms, such as upregulation of prosurvival or anti-apoptotic pathways and enhanced cell adhesion to the extracellular matrix (Gonzalez-Santamarta et al., 2020; Hideshima et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Bortezomib resistance can be attributed to enhanced cell adhesion to the extracellular matrix.
source: Bortezomib resistance can be attributed to targeted mechanisms such as mutations in the bortezomib-binding pocket of the proteasome subunit (PSMB5) and overexpression of proteasome subunits (Barrio et al., 2019; Franke et al., 2012; van de Ven et al., 2008; Wacker et al., 2012) as well as non-specific mechanisms, such as upregulation of prosurvival or anti-apoptotic pathways and enhanced cell adhesion to the extracellular matrix (Gonzalez-Santamarta et al., 2020; Hideshima et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A priori knowledge of tumor cells' susceptibility to candidate therapeutics could aid in identifying effective treatment options, resulting in fewer relapses and failed treatments due to resistance.
source: A priori knowledge of tumor cells' susceptibility to candidate therapeutics could aid in identifying effective treatment options, resulting in fewer relapses and failed treatments due to resistance.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the potential benefits of predicting drug resistance.

claim: Current methods for evaluating drug resistance depend on viability assays and sequencing.
source: However, current methods for evaluating drug resistance depend on viability assays and sequencing, which may be limited in its usefulness without knowledge of the full spectrum of resistance-conferring genomic alterations (Wheler et al., 2014) or knowing specific mutations or indels in the target that suppress drug activity (Kapoor and Miller, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Sequencing may be limited in its usefulness without knowledge of the full spectrum of resistance-conferring genomic alterations.
source: However, current methods for evaluating drug resistance depend on viability assays and sequencing, which may be limited in its usefulness without knowledge of the full spectrum of resistance-conferring genomic alterations (Wheler et al., 2014) or knowing specific mutations or indels in the target that suppress drug activity (Kapoor and Miller, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Methods for determining tumor cell susceptibility prior to therapy are desirable.
source: Methods for determining tumor cell susceptibility prior to therapy are desirable.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the limitations of current methods.

claim: Specific genomic alterations, treatment response, and prognosis can be predicted from conventional hematoxylin and eosin tissue slides using machine learning.
source: A growing literature suggests that specific genomic alterations, treatment response, and prognosis can be predicted from conventional hematoxylin and eosin tissue slides using machine learning (Cifci et al., 2022; Lee and Jang, 2022), indicating that image data holds promise for predicting drug resistance.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Image data holds promise for predicting drug resistance.
source: A growing literature suggests that specific genomic alterations, treatment response, and prognosis can be predicted from conventional hematoxylin and eosin tissue slides using machine learning (Cifci et al., 2022; Lee and Jang, 2022), indicating that image data holds promise for predicting drug resistance.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited literature on machine learning applications to histology images.

claim: High-content microscopy has successfully categorized small molecule inhibitors by their mechanisms and targeted pathways.
source: High-content microscopy, which uses cell-based automated microscopy to capture information-rich images, has successfully categorized small molecule inhibitors by their mechanisms and targeted pathways (Ljosa et al., 2013; Perlman et al., 2004) and shown a relationship between morphological profiles and genetic perturbations (Rohban et al., 2017), including specific mutations associated with lung cancer (Caicedo et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: High-content microscopy has shown a relationship between morphological profiles and genetic perturbations.
source: High-content microscopy, which uses cell-based automated microscopy to capture information-rich images, has successfully categorized small molecule inhibitors by their mechanisms and targeted pathways (Ljosa et al., 2013; Perlman et al., 2004) and shown a relationship between morphological profiles and genetic perturbations (Rohban et al., 2017), including specific mutations associated with lung cancer (Caicedo et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: High-content microscopy has shown a relationship between morphological profiles and specific mutations associated with lung cancer.
source: High-content microscopy, which uses cell-based automated microscopy to capture information-rich images, has successfully categorized small molecule inhibitors by their mechanisms and targeted pathways (Ljosa et al., 2013; Perlman et al., 2004) and shown a relationship between morphological profiles and genetic perturbations (Rohban et al., 2017), including specific mutations associated with lung cancer (Caicedo et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: High-content microscopy has not been used to examine the features of resistance in the absence of drug treatment.
source: However, high-content microscopy has not been used to examine the features of resistance in the absence of drug treatment.
evidence: This statement describes a gap in the literature based on the authors' knowledge.

claim: Cell Painting is a multiplex, fluorescence microscopy assay that labels eight cellular components using six stains imaged in five channels.
source: Here, we used Cell Painting (Bray et al., 2016), a multiplex, fluorescence microscopy assay that labels eight cellular components using six stains imaged in five channels, as an unbiased method to characterize the morphological differences between bortezomib-resistant and -sensitive cancer cells.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the Cell Painting protocol.

claim: Cell Painting labels mitochondria, actin, Golgi, plasma membrane, cytoplasmic RNA, nucleoli, endoplasmic reticulum, and DNA.
source: Cell Painting captures signal in five imaging channels from six fluorescent dyes that stain cells for eight cellular components including mitochondria, actin, Golgi, plasma membrane, cytoplasmic RNA, nucleoli, endoplasmic reticulum, and DNA (Figure 1B; Bray et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the Cell Painting protocol and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: CellProfiler was used to extract single-cell morphological features from individual cells.
source: With these images, we used CellProfiler (Stirling et al., 2021) to extract single-cell morphological features from individual cells.
evidence: This statement describes the methodology used in the study and is supported by a citation.

claim: Approximately 3500 features were extracted from Cell Painting images.
source: The signal from each of the five channels was analyzed in the nucleus, cytoplasm, and total cell and characterized based on features (object parameters) such as signal intensity, shape of the object, texture of the staining pattern, etc. yielding a total of ~3500 features.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the feature extraction process.

claim: Drug-resistant clones were isolated by treating HCT116 parental cells with the desired drug and expanding surviving cells.
source: To isolate drug-resistant clones, we used an approach we have described previously (Kasap et al., 2014; Wacker et al., 2012) and the HCT116 cell line.
evidence: This statement describes the methodology used in the study and is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: HCT116 cells express multidrug resistance pumps at low levels.
source: These cancer cells express multidrug resistance pumps at low levels and are mismatch repair deficient, providing a genetically heterogeneous polyclonal population of cells (Papadopoulos et al., 1994; Teraishi et al., 2005; Umar et al., 1994) allowing for isolation of drug-resistant clones in ~2–3 weeks.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: HCT116 cells provide a genetically heterogeneous polyclonal population of cells.
source: These cancer cells express multidrug resistance pumps at low levels and are mismatch repair deficient, providing a genetically heterogeneous polyclonal population of cells (Papadopoulos et al., 1994; Teraishi et al., 2005; Umar et al., 1994) allowing for isolation of drug-resistant clones in ~2–3 weeks.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Drug-resistant clones can be isolated from HCT116 cells in approximately 2-3 weeks.
source: These cancer cells express multidrug resistance pumps at low levels and are mismatch repair deficient, providing a genetically heterogeneous polyclonal population of cells (Papadopoulos et al., 1994; Teraishi et al., 2005; Umar et al., 1994) allowing for isolation of drug-resistant clones in ~2–3 weeks.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: Rapid selection of resistance could favor the isolation of clones with intrinsic resistance.
source: We hypothesized that a rapid selection of resistance could favor the isolation of clones with intrinsic resistance.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as a hypothesis of the study.

claim: Bortezomib-resistant clones A and E have mutations in PSMB5 identified by RNA sequencing.
source: We also isolated bortezomib-sensitive (wild-type; WT) clones by dilution of the HCT116 parental cell line and acquired two published bortezomib-resistant clones (BZ clones A and E) both with mutations in PSMB5 identified by RNA sequencing performed in previous work (Figure 1—source data 2; Wacker et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work and reference to source data.

claim: The median lethal doses (LD50s) for bortezomib in bortezomib-resistant clones were approximately 2.8- to 9-fold that of HCT116 parental cells.
source: We characterized the bortezomib-resistant clones and found that the median lethal doses (LD50s) for bortezomib were ~2.8- to ~9-fold that of HCT116 parental cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from proliferation assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Bortezomib-sensitive clones had LD50s for bortezomib that ranged from approximately 0.7- to 1.2-fold that of HCT116 parental cells.
source: In contrast, bortezomib-sensitive clones had LD50s for bortezomib that ranged from ~0.7- to~1.2-fold that of HCT116 parental cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from proliferation assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Twelve bortezomib-resistant, five ixazomib-resistant, five CB-5083-resistant, and twelve bortezomib-sensitive clones as well as HCT116 parental cells were used for experiments.
source: Together these methods provided a total of twelve bortezomib-resistant, five ixazomib-resistant, five CB-5083-resistant, and twelve bortezomib-sensitive clones as well as HCT116 parental cells for our experiments.
evidence: This describes the experimental materials used in the study.

claim: Bortezomib-resistant and -sensitive clones treated with taxol had LD50s ranging from approximately 0.6- to 1.9-fold that of HCT116 parental cells.
source: Bortezomib-resistant and -sensitive clones treated with taxol had LD50s ranging from ~0.6- to~1.9-fold that of HCT116 parental cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from proliferation assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Bortezomib-sensitive clones and most bortezomib-resistant clones had similar LD50s when treated with mitoxantrone.
source: Treating cells with mitoxantrone, we found that the bortezomib-sensitive clones (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E) and most of the bortezomib-resistant clones had similar LD50s (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is a result from proliferation assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Bortezomib-resistant clone BZ06 had an LD50 for mitoxantrone nearly 14-fold higher than that of HCT116 parental cells.
source: There was one exception (BZ06) that had an LD50 nearly 14-fold higher than that of HCT116 parental cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from proliferation assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cell Painting captures signal in five imaging channels from six fluorescent dyes.
source: Cell Painting captures signal in five imaging channels from six fluorescent dyes that stain cells for eight cellular components including mitochondria, actin, Golgi, plasma membrane, cytoplasmic RNA, nucleoli, endoplasmic reticulum, and DNA (Figure 1B; Bray et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the Cell Painting protocol and reference to Figure 1B showing the imaging channels.

claim: Cellular heterogeneity within each clone and between clones with similar bortezomib sensitivities was observed.
source: We observed cellular heterogeneity within each clone as well as between clones with similar bortezomib sensitivities (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the microscopy images presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cellular heterogeneity obscured potential morphological differences between clones and prevented qualitative distinction of bortezomib-resistant from -sensitive clones by eye.
source: This heterogeneity obscured any potential morphological differences between clones and prevented us from qualitatively distinguishing bortezomib-resistant from -sensitive clones by eye, supporting the need for high-content quantitative analysis.
evidence: This is an observation from the microscopy images that supports the need for quantitative analysis.

claim: The morphological profiles of bortezomib-resistant and bortezomib-sensitive cells did not cleanly distinguish clones based on bortezomib resistance.
source: The morphological profiles of bortezomib-resistant and bortezomib-sensitive cells did not cleanly distinguish clones based on bortezomib resistance (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a result from the initial analysis of morphological profiles presented in the manuscript.

claim: A short 4 hr treatment with 7 nM bortezomib did not allow distinction of clones based on bortezomib sensitivity.
source: We saw a similar failure to distinguish clones based on bortezomib sensitivity after a short, 4 hr treatment with 7 nM bortezomib (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), suggesting that if there is a morphological difference between bortezomib-resistant and -sensitive cells, further feature refinement would be needed for its identification.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of morphological profiles after drug treatment.

claim: Further feature refinement is needed to identify morphological differences between bortezomib-resistant and -sensitive cells.
source: We saw a similar failure to distinguish clones based on bortezomib sensitivity after a short, 4 hr treatment with 7 nM bortezomib (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), suggesting that if there is a morphological difference between bortezomib-resistant and -sensitive cells, further feature refinement would be needed for its identification.
evidence: This is inferred from the inability to distinguish clones without further analysis.

claim: A linear model was fit to each morphological feature adjusting for technical variables (experimental run/batch, incubation time, cell count/density, clone ID) and biological variables (resistance status).
source: Using bortezomib-sensitive clones WT01-05 and bortezomib-resistant clones BZ01-05 to quantify and reduce the impact of technical variables, we fit a linear model to each morphological feature adjusting for technical variables (experimental run/batch, incubation time, cell count/density, clone ID) and biological variables (resistance status) (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the statistical methodology used in the study.

claim: Morphological features with variances that correlated with experimental run (batch), incubation time, cell density, or those features that varied between two or more pairs of bortezomib-sensitive clones were discarded.
source: We then discarded morphological features with variances that correlated with experimental run (batch), incubation time (4 or 13 hours with 0.1% DMSO), cell density, or those features that varied between two or more pairs of bortezomib-sensitive clones (clone ID) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A-E).
evidence: This describes the feature selection methodology used in the study.

claim: 45 morphological features significantly contributed to a clone's bortezomib resistance.
source: This resulted in 45 morphological features that significantly contributed to a clone's bortezomib resistance (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the feature selection process.

claim: Singscore was used to compute a rank-based resistance score or 'Bortezomib Signature' for each well profile.
source: We used these 45 features to compute a rank-based resistance score or 'Bortezomib Signature' for each well profile based on the direction-sensitive method called singscore (Foroutan et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the methodology used to generate the Bortezomib Signature, supported by a citation.

claim: Singscore calculates a normalized score between -1 and 1, with higher values expected for bortezomib-resistant clones and lower values expected for bortezomib-sensitive clones.
source: Singscore ranks these 45 resistance-related features on a per sample basis and calculates a normalized score between –1 and 1, with higher values expected for bortezomib-resistant clones and lower values expected for bortezomib-sensitive clones.
evidence: This describes the properties of the singscore method.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature features were largely independent, displaying low pairwise correlation, with the exception of some texture-based features.
source: With the exception of some texture-based features, the Bortezomib Signature features were largely independent, displaying low pairwise correlation (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of feature correlations presented in the manuscript.

claim: Radial distribution features were higher in resistant cells.
source: We then examined the grouping of features across compartments and channels and found radial distribution features were higher in resistant cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of feature patterns presented in the manuscript.

claim: The pattern of Bortezomib Signatures did not correspond to well position relative to the plate.
source: We found that the pattern of Bortezomib Signatures did not correspond to well position relative to the plate (Figure 2—figure supplement 6B), indicating that the well position for each clone was not strongly contributing to its Bortezomib Signature.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of potential technical artifacts.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature correlated with the resistance status of clones and not technical variables.
source: In addition, we found that the Bortezomib Signature correlated with the resistance status of clones and not technical variables (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of signature correlations presented in the manuscript.

claim: The analysis pipeline and signature building process minimized technical artifacts.
source: These data suggest that our analysis pipeline and signature building process minimized technical artifacts.
evidence: This is inferred from the results showing no correlation with technical variables.

claim: The data was separated into training, validation, test, and holdout datasets using machine learning best practices.
source: To evaluate the performance of the Bortezomib Signature, we used machine learning best practices, separating our data into training, validation, test, and holdout datasets (Figure 3—source data 1; see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the methodology used to evaluate the signature.

claim: In the training dataset, the Bortezomib Signature correctly predicted the bortezomib resistance of all ten clones.
source: In the training dataset, the Bortezomib Signature correctly predicted the bortezomib resistance of all ten clones, with median Bortezomib Signatures for eight out of ten clones beyond the 95% confidence interval for the randomly permuted data (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on the training dataset.

claim: The accuracy of the Bortezomib Signature was 88% for the training dataset.
source: The accuracy of the Bortezomib Signature was 88% while the average precision was 81% for the training dataset (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B) (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on the training dataset.

claim: The average precision of the Bortezomib Signature was 81% for the training dataset.
source: The accuracy of the Bortezomib Signature was 88% while the average precision was 81% for the training dataset (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B) (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on the training dataset.

claim: In the validation dataset, the Bortezomib Signature had an accuracy of 92% and an average precision of 89%.
source: The signature performed similarly well in the validation dataset (Figure 3B), with an accuracy of 92% and an average precision of 89% (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on the validation dataset.

claim: In the test dataset, the Bortezomib Signature correctly predicted the bortezomib resistance of all clones.
source: In the test dataset the Bortezomib Signature correctly predicted the bortezomib resistance of all clones, although only HCT116 parental cells had a median Bortezomib Signature outside the 95% confidence interval for the randomly permuted data (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a result from the evaluation of the signature on the test dataset.

claim: The test dataset had an accuracy of 80% and an average precision of 68%.
source: The test dataset had an accuracy of 80% and an average precision of 68% (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on the test dataset.

claim: In the holdout dataset, the Bortezomib Signature had an accuracy of 78% and an average precision of 69%.
source: Similarly, in the holdout dataset the Bortezomib Signature had an accuracy of 78% and an average precision of 69% (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B), and correctly predicted the bortezomib resistance of twelve out of thirteen clones, with WT01 misclassified as bortezomib-resistant (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on the holdout dataset.

claim: In the holdout dataset, the Bortezomib Signature correctly predicted the bortezomib resistance of twelve out of thirteen clones, with WT01 misclassified as bortezomib-resistant.
source: Similarly, in the holdout dataset the Bortezomib Signature had an accuracy of 78% and an average precision of 69% (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B), and correctly predicted the bortezomib resistance of twelve out of thirteen clones, with WT01 misclassified as bortezomib-resistant (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a result from the evaluation of the signature on the holdout dataset.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature performed better than random chance in all testing conditions.
source: The Bortezomib Signature performed better than random chance in all testing conditions, as demonstrated by comparison with the mean accuracy and average precision for the randomly shuffled data (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B), and as reflected in receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, which describe the classification trade-off between true positive and false positive rates in predicting bortezomib resistance (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a result from the evaluation of the signature compared to random permutations.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature clusters same-type clones (bortezomib-resistant vs. bortezomib-sensitive) with higher enrichment compared to the full feature space, standard feature selection, or a random selection of 45 features.
source: We then compared our linear-modeling approach to feature selection against other feature spaces and found that the Bortezomib Signature clusters same-type clones (bortezomib-resistant vs. bortezomib-sensitive) with higher enrichment compared to the full feature space, standard feature selection (see Materials and methods), or a random selection of 45 features (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the comparison of different feature selection approaches.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature can distinguish bortezomib-resistant from -sensitive clones better than random chance across datasets.
source: These data are consistent with the Bortezomib Signature being able to distinguish bortezomib-resistant from -sensitive clones better than random chance across datasets.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the evaluation results across multiple datasets.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature performed better than chance at identifying ixazomib-resistant and CB-5083-resistant clones.
source: The Bortezomib Signature performed better than chance at identifying ixazomib-resistant and CB-5083-resistant clones (Figure 4A), correctly identifying four of five ixazomib-resistant clones (Figure 4B) and three of five CB-5083-resistant clones (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a result from the evaluation of the signature on clones resistant to other drugs.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature correctly identified four of five ixazomib-resistant clones.
source: The Bortezomib Signature performed better than chance at identifying ixazomib-resistant and CB-5083-resistant clones (Figure 4A), correctly identifying four of five ixazomib-resistant clones (Figure 4B) and three of five CB-5083-resistant clones (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on ixazomib-resistant clones.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature correctly identified three of five CB-5083-resistant clones.
source: The Bortezomib Signature performed better than chance at identifying ixazomib-resistant and CB-5083-resistant clones (Figure 4A), correctly identifying four of five ixazomib-resistant clones (Figure 4B) and three of five CB-5083-resistant clones (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on CB-5083-resistant clones.

claim: The area under the ROC (AUROC) curve for ixazomib-resistant clones was 0.63.
source: The area under the ROC (AUROC) curve for ixazomib-resistant and CB-5083-resistant clones (0.63 and 0.60, respectively) was lower than those calculated for the training, validation, test, and holdout datasets for bortezomib-resistant clones.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on ixazomib-resistant clones.

claim: The area under the ROC (AUROC) curve for CB-5083-resistant clones was 0.60.
source: The area under the ROC (AUROC) curve for ixazomib-resistant and CB-5083-resistant clones (0.63 and 0.60, respectively) was lower than those calculated for the training, validation, test, and holdout datasets for bortezomib-resistant clones.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on CB-5083-resistant clones.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature is not a general signature of UPS-targeting drug resistance.
source: These results suggest that the Bortezomib Signature is not a general signature of UPS-targeting drug resistance, nor of our cloning protocol, and instead has some specificity for bortezomib.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential performance of the signature on bortezomib versus other UPS-targeting drugs.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature has some specificity for bortezomib.
source: These results suggest that the Bortezomib Signature is not a general signature of UPS-targeting drug resistance, nor of our cloning protocol, and instead has some specificity for bortezomib.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential performance of the signature on bortezomib versus other UPS-targeting drugs.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature had an AUROC of 0.75 for clones not included in the training dataset.
source: The Bortezomib Signature had an AUROC of 0.75, compared to 0.55 for the shuffled data (Figure 5A) and correctly characterized the bortezomib resistance of HCT116 parental cells and our bortezomib-resistant clones A and E, which we included as controls (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on new clones.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature correctly characterized the bortezomib resistance of four out of five bortezomib-resistant clones not included in the training dataset.
source: The Bortezomib Signature also correctly characterized the bortezomib resistance of four out of five bortezomib-resistant clones and three out of five bortezomib-sensitive clones not included in the training dataset (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on new clones.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature correctly characterized the bortezomib resistance of three out of five bortezomib-sensitive clones not included in the training dataset.
source: The Bortezomib Signature also correctly characterized the bortezomib resistance of four out of five bortezomib-resistant clones and three out of five bortezomib-sensitive clones not included in the training dataset (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the evaluation of the signature on new clones.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature consistently misclassified clones WT10, WT15, and BZ06.
source: While the Bortezomib Signature correctly characterized the bortezomib sensitivity of most clones, it consistently misclassified others (WT10, WT15, and BZ06; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a result from the evaluation of the signature on new clones.

claim: Proliferation assays showed that WT10 and WT15 were sensitive to bortezomib while BZ06 was resistant.
source: Proliferation assays conducted in earlier experiments showed that WT10 and WT15 were sensitive to bortezomib while BZ06 was resistant (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is a result from proliferation assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Differences in morphology varied by clone type for misclassified clones, suggesting unique morphology may be driving each misclassification.
source: By comparing these incorrect predictions with high-confidence correct predictions, we observed differences that varied by clone type, suggesting unique morphology may be driving each of these misclassifications (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of misclassified clones.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature is generalizable to clones not included in the training dataset.
source: These results are consistent with the Bortezomib Signature being generalizable to clones not included in the training dataset and suggest that morphological profiling has the potential to identify bortezomib-resistant clones based on the morphological features of cells in the absence of drug treatment.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the evaluation results on new clones.

claim: Morphological profiling has the potential to identify bortezomib-resistant clones based on the morphological features of cells in the absence of drug treatment.
source: These results are consistent with the Bortezomib Signature being generalizable to clones not included in the training dataset and suggest that morphological profiling has the potential to identify bortezomib-resistant clones based on the morphological features of cells in the absence of drug treatment.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the overall results of the study.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature is conceptually similar to the on-disease/off-disease score.
source: The Bortezomib Signature is conceptually similar to the on-disease/off-disease score (Heiser et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Both the Bortezomib Signature and the on-disease/off-disease score require three phenotypic measurements: a target phenotype representing ideal, a disease phenotype, and a new phenotype to classify.
source: Both require three phenotypic measurements: a target phenotype representing ideal, a disease phenotype, and a new phenotype to classify.
evidence: This describes a similarity between the two approaches.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature approach is technically different from the on-disease/off-disease score (non-parametric compared to linear projection).
source: However, our approach is technically different (non-parametric compared to linear projection) and our goals are different (phenotypic classification compared to perturbation alignment).
evidence: This describes a difference between the two approaches.

claim: The goals of the Bortezomib Signature approach are different from the on-disease/off-disease score (phenotypic classification compared to perturbation alignment).
source: However, our approach is technically different (non-parametric compared to linear projection) and our goals are different (phenotypic classification compared to perturbation alignment).
evidence: This describes a difference between the two approaches.

claim: There are morphological features of drug resistance in cells that can be identified using Cell Painting.
source: Our work demonstrates that there are morphological features of drug resistance in cells that can be identified using Cell Painting and provides a reproducible pipeline for generating morphological signatures of drug resistance.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the overall results of the study.

claim: The study provides a reproducible pipeline for generating morphological signatures of drug resistance.
source: Our work demonstrates that there are morphological features of drug resistance in cells that can be identified using Cell Painting and provides a reproducible pipeline for generating morphological signatures of drug resistance.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the overall results of the study.

claim: The Bortezomib Signature misclassified three clones not included in the training dataset.
source: The Bortezomib Signature's performance was not perfect; it misclassified three clones not included in the training dataset.
evidence: This is a result from the evaluation of the signature on new clones.

claim: One of the misclassified clones (BZ06) had reduced sensitivity to mitoxantrone as well as bortezomib.
source: Interestingly, one of the misclassified clones (BZ06) had reduced sensitivity to mitoxantrone as well as bortezomib.
evidence: This is a result from proliferation assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Some misclassified clones may have orthogonal mechanisms of resistance or unrelated mutations contributing to their morphological profiles.
source: Given the considerable genetic heterogeneity in this mismatch repair-deficient HCT116 cell line (Glaab and Tindall, 1997; Umar et al., 1994), it is possible that some misclassified clones have orthogonal mechanisms of resistance or unrelated mutations contributing to their morphological profiles.
evidence: This is speculation based on the known genetic heterogeneity of HCT116 cells and the misclassification results.

claim: Targeted sequencing of the PSMB5 proteasome subunit in bortezomib-resistant clones may provide information regarding origins of misclassifications.
source: Targeted sequencing of the PSMB5 proteasome subunit in bortezomib-resistant clones may provide information regarding origins of these misclassifications, as multiple mutations have been identified in bortezomib-resistant clones (Wacker et al., 2012).
evidence: This is speculation about future experiments that could explain misclassifications, supported by a citation.

claim: Multiple mutations have been identified in bortezomib-resistant clones.
source: Targeted sequencing of the PSMB5 proteasome subunit in bortezomib-resistant clones may provide information regarding origins of these misclassifications, as multiple mutations have been identified in bortezomib-resistant clones (Wacker et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Morphological profiling with Cell Painting can be used as an unbiased method to characterize resistance in the absence of drug treatment.
source: Together, our work demonstrates the potential for morphological profiling with Cell Painting to be used as an unbiased method to characterize resistance in the absence of drug treatment.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the overall results of the study.

claim: Different mechanisms of bortezomib resistance may generate distinct morphological profiles.
source: Our results indicate that different mechanisms of bortezomib resistance may generate distinct morphological profiles; with larger and broader training datasets, it may be possible to identify signatures for distinct mechanisms of bortezomib resistance as well as signatures of resistance to other drugs.
evidence: This is inferred from the results showing specificity of the signature.

claim: With larger and broader training datasets, it may be possible to identify signatures for distinct mechanisms of bortezomib resistance as well as signatures of resistance to other drugs.
source: Our results indicate that different mechanisms of bortezomib resistance may generate distinct morphological profiles; with larger and broader training datasets, it may be possible to identify signatures for distinct mechanisms of bortezomib resistance as well as signatures of resistance to other drugs.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications of the method.

claim: It is unclear whether this method can be extended to patient samples.
source: Although it is unclear whether this method can be extended to patient samples, where identifying intrinsic drug resistance in cells prior to treatment has the potential to improve targeted cancer therapy, our results are an encouraging proof of concept.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation and uncertainty about future applications.

claim: Identifying intrinsic drug resistance in cells prior to treatment has the potential to improve targeted cancer therapy.
source: Although it is unclear whether this method can be extended to patient samples, where identifying intrinsic drug resistance in cells prior to treatment has the potential to improve targeted cancer therapy, our results are an encouraging proof of concept.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the potential clinical impact of the method.

claim: Further refinement may develop Cell Painting as a tool for identifying drug-resistant cells, perhaps even guiding strategies to overcome resistance.
source: We expect that further refinement may develop Cell Painting as a tool for identifying drug-resistant cells, perhaps even guiding strategies to overcome resistance.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications and improvements of the method.

claim: HCT116 cells were purchased from ATCC (CCL-247).
source: HCT116 cells (RRID: CVCL_0291) were purchased from ATCC (CCL-247) and were maintained in McCoy's 5 A Medium (Gibco) supplemented with 10% (v/v) FBS (Sigma) and cultured at 5% CO2 and 37 °C.
evidence: This describes the source and culture conditions of the cell line used in the study.

claim: HCT116 cells were determined to be mycoplasma-free using a PCR-based method.
source: Cells were determined to be mycoplasma-free using a PCR-based method (Uphoff and Drexler, 2013).
evidence: This describes a quality control measure for the cell line, supported by a citation.

claim: CellProfiler versions 3.1.8 and 3.1.9 were used to perform illumination correction, single-cell segmentation, and morphology feature extraction.
source: We used CellProfiler versions 3.1.8 and 3.1.9 (Caicedo et al., 2018) to perform the standard processing pipeline of illumination correction, single-cell segmentation, and morphology feature extraction.
evidence: This describes the software and methods used for image analysis, supported by a citation.

claim: 3,528 total cell morphology features were extracted from all 25,331,572 cells captured in this experiment.
source: We extracted 3,528 total cell morphology features from all 25,331,572 cells we captured in this experiment.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the feature extraction process.

claim: The 3528 features represent stain intensities, stain co-localization, textures, areas, and other patterns extracted from all five imaging channels and different segmentation objects (nuclei, cytoplasm, total cells).
source: The 3528 features represent stain intensities, stain co-localization, textures, areas, and other patterns extracted from all five imaging channels and different segmentation objects (nuclei, cytoplasm, total cells).
evidence: This describes the types of features extracted from the images.

claim: Cytominer-database was used to ingest all single-cell, per-compartment CellProfiler output files.
source: We first used cytominer-database to ingest all single-cell, per-compartment CellProfiler output files (comma separated) to clean column names, evaluate integrity of CellProfiler output CSVs, and output single-cell SQLite files for downstream processing.
evidence: This describes the data processing methodology used in the study.

claim: Pycytominer was used for all image-based profiling pipeline steps.
source: Next, we used pycytominer (github hash c1aa34b641b4e07eb5cbd424166f31355abdbd4d) for all image-based profiling pipeline steps.
evidence: This describes the software used for data processing in the study.

claim: Single cells were median aggregated to form well-level profiles.
source: In the first step, we median aggregated all single cells to form well-level profiles (Way et al., 2022).
evidence: This describes the data processing methodology used in the study, supported by a citation.

claim: Standard z-score normalization was performed to ensure all features are measured on the same scale with zero mean and unit variance.
source: Third, we performed standard z-score normalization to ensure all features are measured on the same scale with zero mean and unit variance.
evidence: This describes the data normalization methodology used in the study.

claim: Feature selection removed features with low variance, high correlation (>0.9 Pearson correlation), features with missing values, features on the blocklist, and features with outliers greater than 15 standard deviations.
source: Lastly, we performed feature selection, which removed features with low variance, high correlation (>0.9 Pearson correlation), features with missing values, features on our blocklist (Way, 2020), and features with outliers greater than 15 standard deviations, which we suspected were measured in error.
evidence: This describes the feature selection methodology used in the study, with a citation for the blocklist.

claim: The final analytical datasets resulted in 782 features after normalization and feature selection.
source: For developing our final analytical datasets (see section, Constructing the resistance signature) we performed normalization within each plate but performed a combined feature selection across all plates per analytical dataset using the same procedures described previously, which resulted in 782 features.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the feature selection process.

claim: Batch effect correction was not applied because large differences in variance attributable to well position and batch were not detected.
source: We did not detect large differences in variance that could be attributed to well position and batch and therefore did not apply batch effect correction.
evidence: This describes a methodological decision based on the analysis of technical variables.
